IP counsel before answering, same as the US flow.

The German form is the Abmahnung with a strafbewehrte Unterlassungserklärung attached: signing that cease-and-desist declaration creates a contract with penalties for every future breach, so never sign it unreviewed. Short stated deadlines are normal and an einstweilige Verfügung (preliminary injunction) can follow quickly — counsel first.

A mise en demeure letter typically precedes a contrefaçon action; preserve your evidence and answer through IP counsel — once litigation starts, saisie-contrefaçon evidence seizures move quickly, so the calm, reasoned reply matters as much as in the US.

A C&D under the Trade Marks Act 1999 works like the US letter — and Section 142 provides a remedy against groundless threats, which a reasoned reply can invoke. Pull the claimed mark's record on the registry before answering, with counsel.

The letter arrives as a carta de interpelação before an infringement action in the specialised IP court — capture its own stated deadline, verify the sender's INPI registrations, and answer through counsel; never ignore it.

Canadian C&Ds work like US ones — a demand with its own deadline, not an order, and no unjustified-threats statute tempers them — so verify the sender's CIPO registrations and respond through counsel before the stated date.

title: Respond to a cease-and-desist
description: A cease-and-desist is a demand, not a court order, but ignoring one is how lawsuits start. Note what they are claiming and the deadline in the letter. There is no statutory response deadline; the letter, and any lawsuit that follows, sets the pace. Preserve your evidence before anything changes. Get IP counsel involved before you reply, admit anything, or sign anything. Your options are three: comply (stop or rebrand), negotiate (coexistence or license), or contest. Educational guidance, not legal advice. The active work is a few founder-hours; the other side's reply time is out of your hands.

nodes.label: Read the letter calmly: who sent it, the exact claims, and its stated response deadline
Preserve the evidence: archive the letter, your first-use dates, sales records, and screenshots
Look up the claimed mark on USPTO TSDR: registration status, goods and services, filing dates
Choose counsel for the response (IP/trademark litigation)
Assess with counsel: their mark's strength, your actual use, and the options — comply, negotiate, or contest
Draft the response (or the rebrand/coexistence plan counsel recommends)
Send the response before the letter's stated deadline
Wait for the counterparty's reply and calendar the follow-through

trigger: Your US visa is stuck (221(g) administrative processing after the interview, or a petition sitting past posted times) while the company needs you in Silicon Valley.
supportReason: The status portals are captcha-gated government surfaces, the 221(g) response and expedite case are judgment calls made with counsel, and a congressional inquiry moves only on your signed privacy release. An agent can draft the expedite memo from your records; it cannot move a consulate.

contextNeeded.query: visa class, case number, and interview/filing dates
evidence for an expedite case (financial loss, emergencies)

geoNotes.summary: Inherently US-inbound: a UK founder hits this situation in the US embassy/consulate queue, not in any UK process — the 221(g) administrative-processing reality this situation maps is the same one from London.

Inherently US-inbound: Indian founders face this situation at the US consulates (where 221(g) administrative processing is famously common), not in any Indian process — the escalation paths are the US ones this situation maps.

Inherently US-inbound: a German founder encounters this situation at the US consulate (Frankfurt handles most visa classes), not in any German process — the delay machinery and its unsticking levers are the US ones mapped here.
Inherently US-inbound: a French founder faces this at the US embassy in Paris, not in a French process — the 221(g) wait and the expedite/inquiry levers are the US-side machinery this situation maps.

Inherently US-inbound: a Portuguese founder hits this situation in the US embassy queue (Lisbon processes most visa classes), not in any Portuguese process — the 221(g) administrative-processing reality is the same one this situation maps.

Inherently US-inbound: a Canadian founder encounters this situation at a US consulate or port of entry (many classes are even adjudicated at the border for Canadians), not in any Canadian process — the unsticking levers are all American.

title: Unstick a delayed US visa
description: You cannot force a stuck visa, only push. First find where it is stuck: CEAC for the consulate, the USCIS case tracker for the petition. With 221(g) administrative processing, know what you are in: no fixed timeline, no appeal. Most cases resolve; some take months. Your moves: a documented expedite request against USCIS's published criteria, Form I-907 premium processing if your petition type qualifies (it does nothing for a consular 221(g)), immigration counsel, and a congressional inquiry with your signed privacy release. Plan B: run the company remotely while you wait. Educational guidance, not legal advice. CEAC and the USCIS tracker sit behind bot walls, so status checks are done by hand, not API.

nodes.label: Check the consular case status on CEAC
Check the petition status on the USCIS case tracker (if a petition underlies your visa)
Identify the hold: 221(g) administrative processing vs a petition backlog vs a missing-document request

nodes.actionLabel: USCIS: how to make an expedite request
nodes.label: Draft the expedite case against the published USCIS criteria (severe financial loss, emergencies, government interest)
File Form I-907 premium processing if your petition classification qualifies (designated I-129/I-140 classes per USCIS)
Engage immigration counsel on the 221(g) response and the escalation paths
Sign the privacy release and open a congressional inquiry through your district office
Set the honest plan B: run the company remotely from your current country until the visa clears
Wait for consular or USCIS action, re-checking status weekly

trigger: You discover unauthorized access to customer or company data: a breach is live or just happened.
supportReason: Containment calls, counsel, statute mapping, and the notifications themselves are human judgment with legal weight. An agent can preserve the forensic evidence and assemble the incident timeline; it cannot decide who must be told what, where.

geoNotes.summary: Under UK GDPR a notifiable personal-data breach must be reported to the ICO without undue delay and within 72 hours of awareness — the ICO's self-assessment and reporting flow is the canonical route.

In Germany GDPR Article 33 applies — report to the competent state data-protection authority within 72 hours of awareness; the federal BfDI fronts the supervisory landscape and routes to the Länder authorities.

India's CERT-In directions require reporting covered cyber incidents within six hours of noticing — far tighter than any US state clock — and the DPDP Act adds personal-data-breach duties toward the Data Protection Board.

GDPR Article 33 in France runs through the CNIL: notify within 72 hours of awareness via the CNIL's online breach-notification teleservice (a two-stage notification is allowed while facts are incomplete), and inform the affected people where the risk to them is high.

GDPR Article 33 applies directly: report a notifiable personal-data breach to the CNPD within 72 hours of awareness and notify affected individuals when the risk is high — the CNPD fronts the national reporting flow.

Under PIPEDA, report breaches posing a real risk of significant harm to the Privacy Commissioner, notify affected individuals, and keep records of every breach for 24 months — Quebec's private-sector law adds its own CAI reporting track.
geoNotes.actionLabel: OPC — respond to a privacy breach

contextNeeded.query: what systems and data were touched, and when

title: Respond to a data breach
description: In the first hours, contain the breach and preserve the evidence. In the first days, get counsel and count deadlines. Every US state has its own breach-notification law (the NCSL survey maps them), some with deadlines in days: California now sets a hard clock (rule card us-ca.breach-notification-timing, residents within 30 calendar days of discovery). Which laws apply depends on where the affected people live, not where your company is. You cannot unsend a notification, so work out the scope first, then notify whoever the statutes require, with counsel. The geo notes cover the non-US equivalents: the UK GDPR's 72-hour ICO deadline, Germany's Article 33 state authorities, India's six-hour CERT-In directions. Educational guidance, not legal advice. These deadlines are statutes; verify each against the relevant state's law with counsel.

nodes.label: Contain the breach: revoke compromised credentials, rotate keys, isolate affected systems
Preserve the forensic evidence: logs, disk images, access records — nothing gets wiped
Assemble the incident timeline and scope: what data, whose, how many records
Engage breach counsel (and your cyber-insurance carrier's hotline if you're covered)
Map the notification clocks: every US state where affected residents live has its own breach statute — some clocks run in days
File the regulator notifications the statutes require (state attorneys general — e.g. California's portal)
Notify the affected individuals per the controlling statutes (content requirements differ by state)
Run the post-incident review and the remediation plan

trigger: An IRS or state tax notice arrives claiming a discrepancy, a balance due, or a missing filing.
supportReason: An agent can pull the period's books and recompute the asserted mismatch; reading the notice, the CPA judgment call, the signed response, and the wait on the IRS's side are human.

contextNeeded.query: the notice itself (code, period, amount, deadline)

geoNotes.summary: HMRC's version is the compliance check or a decision letter — respond by the letter's own date, and if you disagree the route is a statutory review and then an appeal to the tax tribunal, most of it on 30-day windows stated in the decision itself.
geoNotes.actionLabel: HMRC — disagree with a tax decision

geoNotes.summary: A Steuerbescheid from the Finanzamt carries a one-month Einspruch (objection) window under §355 AO — object in time and the assessment stays open while it is re-examined; let the month lapse and it binds. The notice's own Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung states the clock.

A proposition de rectification from the DGFiP opens its own stated reply window (30 days, extendable on request), and the réclamation through your espace professionnel on impots.gouv.fr is the formal contest route — answer by the letter's date, with your accountant.

Income-tax notices (143(1) mismatches, 139(9) defective returns, 142(1) inquiries) land in the e-filing portal's e-Proceedings and are answered there by the notice's own date — the response flow is electronic end to end against your PAN.

An AT assessment or notice carries its own response window: answer through the portal's e-balcão, and if you disagree the formal route is the reclamação graciosa (120 days) and then judicial review — deadlines bind.

A CRA notice of assessment or reassessment is contested by filing a notice of objection within 90 days of the notice date — respond inside the window or the assessment binds; the CRA's disputes flow is online.

title: Answer an IRS or state tax notice
description: Most tax notices are not audits. They point at one mismatch and print a response deadline on the first page (rule card us-fed.cp2000-response-deadline: the CP2000 reply is due by the date listed on the notice). Read the notice code, pull that period's records, and recompute the number they claim is wrong. Then respond by the deadline: agree and pay, or contest with documentation (the IRS document upload tool covers many notice types). If the response needs a signed statement, the signature is yours, sometimes under penalty of perjury. Educational guidance, not legal advice. The deadline that matters is printed on your notice; verify it there.

nodes.actionLabel: IRS: understanding your notice or letter
nodes.label: Read the notice: the notice code (CP/LTR), tax period, amount claimed, and its printed response deadline
Pull the period's records from your books: the filed return, payroll filings, ledger detail
Recompute what the notice asserts against what you filed — most notices are one specific mismatch
Engage your CPA (or tax counsel if the amount or issue is material)
Respond by the notice's deadline: agree and pay, or contest with documentation
Sign the response where the notice requires a signed statement (some are made under penalty of perjury)
If you disagree with the outcome, weigh an appeal with your CPA
Wait for the IRS or state to process the response

trigger: Your operating account is frozen by the bank's compliance review, or the bank itself fails.
supportReason: Opening the backup account is KYC-gated, the freeze conversation is with the bank's compliance team, and the FDIC claim is theirs to process. An agent can size the insurance exposure from your balances; it cannot unfreeze an account.

contextNeeded.query: which bank, which accounts, and current balances
the next payroll date and critical payment schedule

geoNotes.summary: If a UK-authorised bank fails, the FSCS protects £85,000 per depositor per bank and aims to pay most depositors within days; a compliance freeze is the same KYC/UBO documents conversation with the bank — and standing up a second operating account for payroll is the same first move.

The statutory Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken (EdB) compensates €100,000 per depositor per bank (the EU deposit-guarantee floor) and contacts depositors after a failure; compliance freezes are worked out with the bank's own team under BaFin supervision.

The FGDR guarantees €100,000 per depositor per bank and targets compensation within seven working days of a failure; a gel du compte lifts on the bank's KYC questions being answered, not on a form — the backup-account move is identical.

DICGC insurance covers ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (principal plus interest), and RBI moratoria on stressed banks have historically capped withdrawals for months — which makes the second-account triage even more important than in the US.

title: Recover from a frozen bank account or bank failure
description: Frozen account or failed bank, the problem is the same: payroll has to go out, in every country. Confirm what happened. Work out how much is covered by deposit insurance (US: FDIC covers $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category; the UK, German, French, and Indian caps are in the geo notes). Open a second operating account so the payments that cannot bounce don't. Then the paths split. A compliance freeze is a documents conversation with the bank: KYC and beneficial ownership. A bank failure is a receivership you track and file claims against for the uninsured balance (in the US, with the FDIC). Moving banking rails mid-crisis can be undone, but at real cost.

nodes.label: Confirm what happened: a compliance freeze notice from the bank, or the bank itself failing (US: the FDIC failed-bank list; your country's resolution authority otherwise)
Size the exposure: balances against your deposit-protection limit (US: FDIC's $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category — other schemes in the geo notes)
Triage the next payroll run and the payments that cannot bounce
Open a backup operating account at a second bank
Re-point the rails: processor payouts in, payroll and vendor payments out
If it's a compliance freeze: ask what triggered the review and supply the KYC/UBO documents the bank asks for
If the bank failed: track the receivership (US: the FDIC's) and file the claim for uninsured balances
Wait for the freeze review or the receivership distributions

trigger: Your dispute rate jumps: a chargeback wave or a card-testing/fraud spike is hitting your payments.
supportReason: Dispute data, fraud rules, evidence submission, and refunds are real API surfaces on the judged processors, so an agent can run most of the loop. Pausing a product surface and the monitoring-program judgment stay human.

contextNeeded.query: processor account access and the dispute window to analyze

title: Contain a chargeback or fraud spike
description: Most of this runs through your processor's APIs. Quantify the pattern. Tighten your fraud rules. Contest the disputes worth contesting; each card network has its own process and deadlines. Refund obvious fraud before it becomes a chargeback. A refund costs less than a lost dispute, and a sent refund cannot be undone, so refunds sit behind an approval step. The card networks' monitoring programs have thresholds with real consequences; watching them with your processor is the judgment part.

nodes.label: Quantify the spike: dispute rate, affected charges, and the common pattern (BIN, geography, velocity)
Tighten the fraud rules: raise risk thresholds, require 3DS where it applies
Pause the leaking surface if the pattern demands it (a SKU, a geo, a payment method)
Submit evidence on the disputes worth contesting — responses are per-network and deadline-bound
Refund clear fraud before it becomes a chargeback — a refund costs less than a lost dispute
Watch the card networks' monitoring-program thresholds with your processor
Wait for the dispute outcomes and re-read the rate weekly

trigger: A co-founder is leaving (resignation or a split) and the vesting, IP, and access mechanics start now.
supportReason: The board consent and the repurchase are signature acts with closing windows, and the departure terms are negotiated between people. An agent can run the vesting math, the access revocation, and the cap-table update.

contextNeeded.query: the stock purchase agreement (vesting schedule, repurchase window)

geoNotes.summary: The mechanics run through Companies House (TM01 for the directorship, PSC updates where ownership crosses thresholds) and through the articles and shareholders' agreement — good-leaver/bad-leaver provisions usually decide what happens to the shares and at what price.

GmbH shares move only by notarized deed (§15 GmbHG — the Abtretung requires notarielle Beurkundung) and the updated Gesellschafterliste is filed to the Handelsregister; founder vesting lives in the Gesellschaftervereinbarung, not in statute, so read yours first.

In a SAS the statuts and the pacte d'associés govern the exit (leaver and forced-transfer clauses); the share movement is recorded in the company's registre de mouvements de titres and officer changes file through the INPI guichet unique.

Director changes file to the RoC on DIR-12 within 30 days (the director's own DIR-11 alongside), share transfers move on Form SH-4 with stamp duty, and founder vesting is a shareholders'-agreement matter enforced through the articles — same mechanics, MCA paperwork.

The exit runs through the acordo parassocial's leaver clauses: quota transfers need written form and registration (no notary since 2006), the registry record is updated online, and the vesting/clawback math is whatever the agreement wrote down.

The USA's leaver provisions govern: vested vs unvested shares at the departure date, a directors' resolution for any repurchase, updated share registers — and since 2024 CBCA corporations also file individuals-with-significant-control changes.

title: Handle a co-founder departure
description: Three things protect the company: the vesting math, a board consent, and a deadline. Calculate vested versus unvested shares at the departure date. Have the board accept the resignation and authorize the repurchase of unvested shares. Exercise it inside the window your stock agreement sets, often 90 days from termination; read yours. Confirm the signed IP assignment is on file. Revoke access the same day. Update the cap table. Tell the team once, clearly. Separation agreements and releases are work for employment counsel. Once executed, the repurchase and board consent cannot be undone. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

nodes.label: Agree the departure date and terms in writing
Run the vesting math: shares vested vs unvested at the departure date
Board consent: accept the resignation, remove officer roles, authorize the unvested-share repurchase
Exercise the repurchase inside the stock-agreement window (often 90 days from termination — the window lapses)
Confirm the IP position: the signed PIIA is on file and the departing founder's work is assigned
Revoke access the same day: workspace, repos, bank, infra — the offboarding checklist
Update the cap table and the stakeholder records
Tell the team (and investors where material) — one honest message

trigger: You've been served: a process server hands you a summons and complaint naming the company.
supportReason: Litigation strategy, the insurer conversations, and the signed, filed pleadings are counsel work under court rules. An agent can stand up the litigation hold across your systems; it cannot answer a complaint.

contextNeeded.query: the summons and complaint, and the date/manner of service

geoNotes.summary: Served with a claim form, you acknowledge service and file a defence on the CPR clock — 14 days from the particulars of claim, 28 with an acknowledgment of service; money claims respond online, and silence ends in default judgment.
geoNotes.actionLabel: gov.uk — respond to a court claim

geoNotes.summary: A served Klage comes with the court's own stated deadlines — typically two weeks to declare the intent to defend (Verteidigungsanzeige) and a further period for the Klageerwiderung; before the Landgericht a lawyer is mandatory (Anwaltszwang), and a missed response risks a Versäumnisurteil.

An assignation names the court and the clock; before the tribunal judiciaire you generally must appoint an avocat (constitution d'avocat) within the summons's stated window — the document itself states your deadline, and default judgment follows silence.

A summons under the CPC sets the date to appear and file the written statement — 30 days, extendable to 90 (and a hard 120-day cap in commercial suits under the Commercial Courts Act); the e-Courts services track the case number end to end.

A served citação starts the clock: the contestação (defence) is typically due within 30 days in ordinary civil proceedings, filed by counsel through the courts' electronic system — the justice portal is the entry point.

Civil procedure is provincial: the summons states your deadline (Ontario gives 20 days from service in-province for a statement of defence) — retain provincial counsel immediately and preserve documents from day one.

title: Respond to a lawsuit
description: Being served starts a real deadline. In federal court the answer is due 21 days after service (FRCP 12(a)(1)(A)(i), rule card us-fed.frcp-answer-deadline); state courts set their own, and your summons states yours. In the first week: record how you were served, calendar the deadline, issue a litigation hold (destroying evidence after that is sanctionable), notify any insurer that might owe you a defense, and engage litigation counsel. The response itself, answer, motion, or negotiate, is your lawyer's craft, filed under FRCP 11's signature rule. Educational guidance, not legal advice. The deadline math has exceptions (waived service, the United States as a party); verify with counsel against the rule.

nodes.label: Record exactly when and how you were served — the answer clock starts at service
Calendar the answer deadline: 21 days in federal court (FRCP 12(a)(1)(A)(i)); state courts differ — the summons states yours
Issue the litigation hold: preserve documents, chat, email — spoliation is sanctionable
Notify your insurers — D&O, E&O, or CGL may owe you a defense
Decide the response with counsel: answer, motion, or negotiate
Counsel files the response before the deadline (every pleading is signed — FRCP 11)
Wait for the next docket event

trigger: The USPTO examiner issues an office action against your trademark application: refusals or requirements with a response deadline.
supportReason: Likelihood-of-confusion arguments are legal craft and the TEAS filing carries the applicant's or attorney's signature. An agent can pull the cited marks' TSDR records; the response is human work.

contextNeeded.query: the office action (serial number, issue date, refusal grounds)

geoNotes.summary: The UKIPO issues an examination report with a two-month response window — objections commonly on distinctiveness, plus notifications of earlier marks surfaced in the search (the UK notifies rather than refuses on relative grounds). Respond, amend, or let it lapse.

A DPMA Beanstandung names the defect (absolute grounds, classification, formalities) with its own stated response deadline; relative grounds arrive later as oppositions after publication — answer through the DPMA's procedures or counsel, inside the stated window.

INPI examination raises objections with the notification's own reply deadline, and third-party oppositions run on fixed windows after publication — both are answered through the INPI e-procedures portal, which is also where the file's status lives.

The registry's examination report must be answered within 30 days of receipt or the application is treated as abandoned — the report and the application status live on the registry's online search, and responses go through an agent or attorney.

INPI raises refusals and irregularities with its own stated response deadline, and published applications face a two-month opposition window — answer through INPI's online services, with counsel for substantive refusals.

A CIPO examiner's report names the objections (confusion, descriptiveness, formalities) with its own stated response deadline — answer every ground through CIPO's online channel or the application lapses.

title: Respond to a trademark office action
description: An office action is a letter from the USPTO examiner, not a rejection of your company. It raises refusals (likelihood of confusion, descriptiveness) or requirements, and each needs an answer. You have three months from the issue date plus one paid three-month extension. Madrid Section 66(a) filings get six months and no extension (rule card us-fed.trademark-office-action-response, USPTO guidance cited). Miss the deadline and the application abandons. Pull the cited marks on TSDR. Decide: argue, amend, or hire counsel. File the signed response in TEAS. This is what happens when the filing from 'File trademark' comes back with questions. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

nodes.label: Read the office action: substantive refusals (likelihood of confusion, descriptiveness) vs procedural requirements
Calendar the deadline: 3 months from the issue date, one 3-month paid extension (Madrid §66(a): 6 months, no extension)
Pull the examiner's cited marks on TSDR and check their live status
Decide the response: argue, amend the application, or bring in trademark counsel
Draft the response and its evidence
Sign and file the response in TEAS before the deadline
Wait for the examiner: approval, a final action, or new issues

trigger: A Delaware delinquency notice arrives: the March 1 annual report/franchise tax was missed and good standing is gone or going.
supportReason: Delaware's filing and payment run through the state's own portal (no public filing API); an agent can recompute the assumed-par-value math and fix the reminder calendar.

contextNeeded.query: the delinquency notice and your file number
issued and authorized share counts + gross assets (for the recompute)

geoNotes.summary: The analog is the overdue confirmation statement or accounts at Companies House: late accounts trigger automatic penalties (from £150, doubled when late two years running) and a long-overdue confirmation statement starts the strike-off path — cure by filing online, then fix the reminders.

Miss the Offenlegung (disclosure) of annual accounts and the Bundesamt für Justiz opens Ordnungsgeld proceedings — from €2,500, repeatable, after a six-week grace notice — so the cure is filing in the Unternehmensregister before the next escalation.

The analog is the overdue dépôt des comptes annuels at the greffe: the president of the tribunal de commerce can order the filing under daily penalty (astreinte), and the cure is simply depositing the accounts through the one-stop formalities channel.

MCA's annual filings (AOC-4 accounts, MGT-7 annual return) accrue additional fees of ₹100 per day per form once late — no cap — and persistent default risks director disqualification; the cure is filing the overdue forms with the accrued fees.

The delinquency analog is a missed IES or Modelo 22: tax-authority fines (coimas) follow and the registry record goes stale — the cure is filing the overdue declarations through the portal, with reduced fines for voluntary regularisation.

Miss the Corporations Canada annual return and the corporation drifts toward administrative dissolution — the cure is filing the overdue return online (and a dissolved corporation can be revived, at more cost and paperwork).

title: Cure a Delaware franchise tax delinquency
description: Missing the March 1 annual report and franchise tax (rule card us-de.franchise-tax-annual-report, 8 Del. C. §§ 502, 504) costs a $200 penalty plus 1.5% monthly interest, and the company falls out of good standing. That blocks fundraising diligence and good-standing certificates until you fix it. Fixing it is mechanical. Before paying the authorized-shares bill, recompute with the assumed-par-value method. File the overdue report, pay online, confirm standing is restored, fix your calendar. The deadline and amounts come from the statute; verify on the state's own pages.

nodes.label: Read the notice: the missed March 1 filing brings a $200 penalty, 1.5%/month interest, and loss of good standing
Recompute the tax with the assumed-par-value method before panicking at the authorized-shares number
File the overdue annual report and pay online
Confirm good standing is restored on the state's entity search
Fix the root cause: calendar March 1 and confirm your registered agent's reminders reach you

trigger: Traffic spikes take the product down: a DDoS attack is live, or a major outage looks like one.
supportReason: Edge mitigation, WAF rules, and status updates are real API surfaces on the judged edge platforms, so an agent can drive them. Incident command, the block-what judgment, and customer communication stay human.

contextNeeded.query: edge/DNS provider account and current traffic picture

title: Survive a DDoS attack or major outage
description: In the first minutes, pick one incident commander and one channel. Then work out what you are in: a volumetric L3/4 flood, an application-layer attack, or a self-inflicted outage that looks like one. Edge mitigation and WAF rules can be agent-driven on the judged edge platforms. What stays human: deciding what to block, talking to customers, the postmortem (its own process: 'Run an incident postmortem'). While an attack is live, a current status page beats silence.

nodes.label: Declare the incident: one commander, one channel, sev1 rules
Identify what you're in: a volumetric L3/4 flood, an L7 application attack, or a self-inflicted outage
Turn on the edge's DDoS mitigation / under-attack mode
Rate-limit and block the attack signatures (WAF rules, geo blocks, bot rules)
Post the status page update — early, honest, updated often
Tell the affected customers: support channels, and the key accounts directly
Stand down and run the postmortem (its own process: 'Run an incident postmortem')

trigger: A vendor you depend on announces a shutdown or sunsets the product you're built on.
supportReason: Exports, imports, and integration re-pointing are agent-drivable where the APIs exist; the replacement choice, the parallel-run judgment, and the cutover call are the founder's.

contextNeeded.query: the shutdown notice (dates, export window) and what depends on the vendor

title: Migrate off a shutting-down vendor
description: You did not choose this deadline, but you have to meet it. The notice gives an end-of-service date and a shorter data-export window. Export your data first, whatever else slips; it is the one step that cannot wait. Then run an ordinary migration under time pressure: pick a replacement from the current market, set it up, run old and new in parallel through one business cycle, cut over. Cancel only after that, and get written confirmation your data was deleted. That confirmation cannot be taken back, which is why it comes last.

nodes.label: Read the shutdown notice: the end-of-service date, the data-export window, and what your contract promises
Export your data now — not in the deadline crunch
Choose the replacement from the live market
Migrate: stand up the replacement, import the data, re-point the integrations
Run and verify the parallel-run window
Review the parallel-run results and cut over
Cancel the old contract and get the data deletion confirmed in writing

trigger: Your payment processor emails that your account is terminated or restricted; payouts pause and a final processing date is set.
supportReason: Data export and the checkout re-point are real API work while access lasts; the appeal, the underwriting conversation at the next processor, and the reserve hold are up to the processors and their timelines.

contextNeeded.query: the termination notice (reason, final processing date, reserve terms)
what runs on the processor: subscriptions, payout cadence, integrations

title: Recover from a payment-processor account termination
description: Your processor is terminating the account. Read the notice: the stated reason, the final processing date, the reserve terms. Processors commonly hold funds against future disputes for a stated period after termination; Stripe's services agreement is public and explains its reserve mechanics, so read yours. Then do three things at once. Export every record while you still have API access. Appeal through the processor's review channel with real evidence. Start underwriting at a backup processor now; onboarding takes days. Moving card data between PCI-compliant processors at the PAN level is a real, supported path, not a workaround. If payouts or renewals will wobble, tell your customers. How long the reserve is held is the processor's call; treat it as a wait.

nodes.label: Read the termination notice: the stated reason, the final processing date, and the reserve/payout-hold terms your services agreement sets
Export everything while API access lasts: charges, customers, subscription state, dispute history, payout records
File the appeal through the processor's own review channel, with evidence: business model, fulfillment proof, dispute history
Choose the backup processor and start its underwriting now — onboarding/KYC runs in days, not hours
Request the PAN-level card-data migration to the new processor (a PCI-compliant processor-to-processor transfer)
Re-point checkout, billing, and webhooks to the new processor behind a flag, and reconcile the first live charges
Tell affected customers honestly if payouts, refunds, or renewals will wobble during the cutover
Wait out the appeal decision and the reserve release — both run on the processor's stated schedule

trigger: A security researcher (or a customer, or a stranger) reports a vulnerability in your product, responsibly so far.
supportReason: Reproduction, the patch loop, and the advisory mechanics are agent-drivable, with the judged scanners gating the fix; the severity call, the disclosure decision, and the reporter relationship stay human.

contextNeeded.query: the vulnerability report itself (vector, affected surface, reporter contact)
access to the affected code and deployment

title: Handle a security-vulnerability report
description: Someone who reports a vulnerability in good faith is doing you a favor. Don't make them wait. Reply fast and open a private channel; ignored researchers go public. Reproduce the bug as they described it. Judge severity by exploitability, not embarrassment. Fix it on the timeline the severity justifies. Agree a disclosure date with the reporter (90-day coordinated disclosure is industry practice, not law) and publish the advisory with credit. Follow CISA's coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure guidance. A security.txt file sends the next report to you instead of your CEO's inbox. If the hole was exploited and data was reached, switch to 'Respond to a data breach': different situation, statutory deadlines.

nodes.label: Acknowledge receipt fast and open a private channel with the reporter — silence is how disclosures go public
Reproduce the report and scope the vulnerable surface: what's reachable, since when, by whom
Make the severity call: drop everything or schedule — exploitability and exposure, not embarrassment
Patch, regression-test, and run the scanners over the fix before it ships
Decide disclosure with the reporter: coordinated timeline, customer notice if data was reachable — exploited means the breach situation instead
Publish the fix and the advisory, credit the reporter, and adopt security.txt so the next report routes cleanly
Hold the coordinated-disclosure window: the fix soaks in production, the reporter holds publication, you re-test

trigger: Someone exercises their data rights: a GDPR subject access request or CCPA request to know/delete lands in any inbox.
supportReason: The data inventory and the export assembly are agent work across your own systems; identity verification judgment, the exemptions review, and the decision to send are human, counsel's where it's close.

geoNotes.summary: UK GDPR's subject access request runs on the same one-month clock with the same two-month extension — the ICO's right-of-access guidance is the canonical employer-side playbook, including the identity-check and exemptions reality.

contextNeeded.query: the request itself and the date it was received (the clock runs from receipt)
where personal data lives: your systems and processors

title: Answer a data-subject access request
description: A DSAR looks like an ordinary email. It is a legal request with a statutory deadline. Under GDPR, respond without undue delay and within one month of receipt. You can extend two more months for complex or numerous requests, but only if you tell the requester within the first month (Art. 12(3), rule card eu.gdpr-dsar-response-deadline, EUR-Lex cited). The CCPA gives you 45 days, per the California AG's own page. Verify the requester's identity proportionately. Inventory everything you hold on them: product database, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor. Have counsel check the exemptions before anything goes out. An over-disclosure cannot be taken back, which is why sending is the irreversible step. Where the request is, or includes, deletion (GDPR Art. 17 erasure, CCPA request to delete), the same clock applies: execute the erasure across systems and processors, apply the statutory exceptions, and confirm what was deleted. Educational guidance, not legal advice; the controlling deadline is the statute's, verified at the primary source.

nodes.label: Log the request and start the clock: one month under GDPR Art. 12(3), 45 days under CCPA — the extension needs notice inside month one
Verify the requester's identity proportionately — enough to stop impersonation, never a data grab of its own
Inventory where this person's data lives: product DB, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor
Assemble the export and draft the response: what you hold, purposes, recipients, retention, sources
Review the exemptions with privacy counsel where it's close: third-party data, privilege, trade secrets
Deliver securely by the deadline and record what was sent (or send the extension notice inside month one)
Fix the intake: a records-of-processing map and a standing DSAR runbook so the next one is routine

Execute the deletion where the request asks for erasure: delete or de-identify across your systems and processors, apply the statutory exceptions (GDPR Art. 17(3), CCPA §1798.105(d)), and record what was deleted and what was retained and why

edges.when: The request seeks access: a copy of the data and the processing details (a request to know).
The request is, or includes, deletion: a GDPR Art. 17 erasure request or a CCPA request to delete.

trigger: Your app is rejected in review, or pulled from the App Store or Google Play with a policy notice.
supportReason: Review and appeals run inside Apple's and Google's own consoles on their own judgment. An agent can diff your build against the cited guideline and assemble the evidence; the appeal and the resubmission decisions are yours.

contextNeeded.query: the rejection/removal notice (guideline or policy cited)
how much of your revenue and install base rides the affected store

title: Recover from an app-store rejection or removal
description: A rejection names a guideline; a removal names a policy. Read which one you got. Apple publishes its App Review guidelines and an appeal path (disagreements go to the App Review Board); Google Play publishes its removal reasons and appeal process in the Play Console help. Usually, fixing the issue and resubmitting beats contesting, unless the reviewer is actually wrong about your app. If store revenue matters, tell your users what is happening while the review runs. How long review takes is the stores' call; treat it as a wait.

nodes.label: Read the rejection/removal notice: which guideline or policy is cited, and what exactly the reviewer saw
Diff your build and metadata against the cited guideline and assemble the evidence: screens, flows, policy docs
Decide the fork: fix and resubmit, or contest — contest only when the reviewer is genuinely wrong about your app

nodes.actionLabel: Apple: appeal an App Review decision
nodes.label: Apple path: resubmit the fixed build, or appeal to the App Review Board through the published flow
Google Play path: follow the published removal/appeal flow in the Play Console help
If store revenue is material, tell users honestly what's happening and what still works
Wait for the review decision — the clock is the stores'

edges.when: The rejection or removal is on Apple's App Store.
The rejection or removal is on Google Play.

trigger: Google Ads, Meta, or another ad/platform account is suspended: campaigns stop and a policy email names the violation.
supportReason: Policy enforcement and appeals run on the platforms' own judgment and consoles; an agent can audit the likely trigger and keep the owned channels running, but deciding what to fix and what to assert in the appeal is on the founder.

contextNeeded.query: the suspension notice (policy cited, account level)
how much acquisition rides the suspended channel

title: Recover a suspended ad or platform account
description: Losing an ad account cuts a growth channel overnight. The appeal that works is filed after the violation is fixed, not before. Read which policy they cited (Google Ads publishes its suspension reasons and appeal path; Meta's runs through the Business Help Center's account-quality flow). Audit what plausibly tripped it: billing mismatches, landing-page policy, circumventing-systems flags. Fix that first. Then file one complete appeal; five thin ones read as circumvention. While the appeal runs, move spend to channels you own, starting with your email list. Reinstatement is the platform's decision; nothing here promises it.

nodes.label: Read the suspension notice: which policy is cited, and at what level (account, campaign, payment profile)
Audit what could have tripped it: billing mismatches, destination/landing-page policy, circumventing-systems flags
Fix the underlying violation first — appeals filed with the violation still live get denied
File ONE complete appeal through the published flow with the fix documented (Meta's path runs through the Business Help Center's account-quality flow)
Shift spend to the channels still standing while the appeal runs — the email list first; concentration was the real lesson
Wait for the appeal decision — the clock is the platform's

trigger: Your domain, DNS, or a company social/email account is taken over: logins fail, records change, or posts you didn't write appear.
supportReason: Recovery runs through registrar cases, ICANN processes, and platform flows that verify the human owner; an agent can run the lock-down, the RDAP checks, and the hardening, but the ownership proofs are yours.

contextNeeded.query: which accounts/domains are affected and what still logs in
registrar, DNS host, and the ownership proofs you hold

title: Recover a hijacked domain or social account
description: The first hour decides how far this spreads. Work out what was taken: the registrar account, DNS, email, or the social handle. Changed MX and DNS records are how one stolen login becomes all of them. Lock what you still hold: passwords, hardware-key 2FA, the registrar transfer lock. Then use the owners' own processes: the registrar's compromise case (if the domain was transferred away, ICANN's transfer-dispute path, where the 60-day rules matter) and the platforms' recovery flows (Google's hacked-account flow; Instagram's /hacked; X's sits behind its help center). Check registration state on RDAP instead of guessing. If posts went out or mail was read, tell the people affected before the screenshots do. A domain transferred to another registrar comes back only with pain.

nodes.label: Scope the compromise: registrar account, DNS, email, or the social handle — and whether MX/DNS were changed (that's how everything else falls)
Lock what you still hold: rotate passwords, enforce hardware-key 2FA, check DNS and MX against known-good, enable the registrar/transfer lock
Open the registrar's compromise case — and if the domain was transferred away, invoke ICANN's transfer-dispute path (the 60-day rules matter)
Verify the live registration state and transfer timeline on RDAP — facts, not guesses
Run the platform's own recovery flow for hijacked accounts (Google's hacked-account flow; Instagram's /hacked; X's via its help center)
If posts went out from your handle or mail was read, tell the people affected before the screenshots do
Harden after recovery: registrar lock + hardware keys everywhere + DNS monitoring, documented
Wait out the registrar/platform case queues and re-verify on RDAP when they close

trigger: A key employee resigns: notice is in hand and the transition starts now.
supportReason: The conversations (resignation, transition, exit interview) are irreducibly human; an agent can run the vesting math, draft the exercise-window notice, and execute the last-day offboarding checklist.

geoNotes.summary: Notice is statutory and contractual: a week's statutory minimum after a month's service, with contracts usually setting more — ACAS's notice-period guidance is the reference — and EMI options carry their own post-cessation tax rules, so the written-window step matters just as much.

Kündigungsfristen are statutory — §622 BGB sets four weeks to the 15th or month-end as the baseline, lengthening with tenure — and termination/resignation requires wet-ink written form (§623 BGB), so the paper is law, not courtesy.

The préavis comes from the convention collective more than the Code du travail — check your branch agreement — and the exit paperwork is mandatory: solde de tout compte, certificat de travail, and the attestation France Travail.

Notice runs off the employment contract and the state's Shops & Establishments Act; the full-and-final settlement timeline and gratuity after five years' service are the statutory tail — the labour ministry is the canonical starting point.

Resignation notice is statutory under the Código do Trabalho — 30 days up to two years of service, 60 days beyond — so the exit timeline is largely fixed by law; confirm equity-plan leaver terms and IP assignment on the way out.

No statutory resignation schedule in most provinces — the contract and common-law reasonable notice govern — while federally regulated employers follow the Canada Labour Code; the protective mechanics are the same offboarding checklist.

contextNeeded.query: the resignation terms: last day and what was agreed
the option grant and plan documents (vesting, post-termination window)

title: Handle a key employee's resignation
description: This is not the co-founder split; that is its own situation. This is the senior engineer or first AE handing in notice. Decide on the merits: counter, or accept a clean exit. Check what the offer letter and handbook say about notice (the US baseline is at-will; your real leverage is goodwill and a good transition plan). Run the equity math. Put the post-termination exercise window in writing to the departing employee. Plans commonly give 90 days, and ISOs lose their tax treatment if exercised more than 3 months after employment ends (IRS Topic 427 cited); a missed window is the classic post-exit dispute. Then knowledge transfer to named successors, same-day offboarding on the last day with final wages on the state's clock (in California, due at quitting after 72 hours' notice, or within 72 hours of a no-notice quit; rule card us-ca.final-wages-timing, Labor Code §§ 202, 203), an exit interview that tells you why people actually leave, and the cap-table and rotation updates. Educational guidance, not legal or tax advice.

nodes.label: Take the resignation conversation properly: last day, transition shape, and whether a counter or a clean exit is honest
Confirm the notice terms from the offer letter and handbook — at-will is the US baseline, so goodwill and the transition plan are the real levers
Run the equity math: vested vs unvested at the last day, and the plan's post-termination exercise window
Put the exercise window in writing to the departing employee — a missed window (and the ISO 3-month rule) is the classic post-exit dispute
Plan the knowledge transfer: owned systems, in-flight work, credentials inventory, named successors
Offboard on the last day: access revocation, device return, final pay on the state's required timeline
Run the exit interview — the honest 30 minutes that tells you why people actually leave
Update the cap table, the org chart, and the on-call rotations

trigger: The lead pulls the term sheet, by call or by silence, and the round you planned around is gone.
supportReason: The investor conversations and the path decision are founder work; an agent can re-run the runway scenarios from the books and rebuild the pipeline and data room for the re-opened process.

contextNeeded.query: the signed term sheet (no-shop/confidentiality terms and dates)
current cash, burn, and committed-but-unclosed checks

title: Absorb a pulled term sheet
description: Start with facts. Get the real reason if you can; a fixable diligence finding is different from partner politics or a turning market. Check what you signed. Term sheets are mostly non-binding except exclusivity/no-shop and confidentiality, so note when the no-shop expires before re-opening conversations (the NVCA model documents show the standard shape). Re-run the runway math on real numbers. Then pick a path: re-open the process wide, bridge with insiders on SAFEs (YC's published documents are the standard), or cut to default-alive. Tell the waiting investors the truth: the round changed, the company did not. If cash is the issue, start the cost plan now; the weeks in denial are the expensive ones. Editorial guidance from the standard documents; nothing here is legal or financial advice.

nodes.label: Get the real reason if you can — a fixable diligence finding, partner politics, or the market are three different problems
Check what you signed: term sheets are mostly non-binding except exclusivity/no-shop and confidentiality — note when the no-shop expires
Re-run the runway on real numbers: months left, the cut scenarios, the honest minimum raise
Pick the path: re-open the process wide, bridge with insiders on SAFEs, or cut to default-alive
Tell the other investors who were waiting, honestly — the round changed, the company didn't
Rebuild the raise machine: refresh the data room, the target list, and the weekly cadence
If cash is the issue, start the cost plan now — the weeks of denial are the expensive part

trigger: Someone is hurt at work: an injury on the job just happened and reporting deadlines may already be running.
supportReason: The emergency response, the carrier conversation, and the return-to-work plan are human; an agent can draft the incident record, keep the OSHA log, and track the claim's deadlines. Treat the state-fund specifics as needs-review until checked against your state.

geoNotes.summary: RIDDOR makes certain workplace injuries reportable to the HSE — deaths and specified injuries by the quickest practicable means with the report within 10 days, over-seven-day incapacitations within 15 — through the HSE's online reporting forms.

Arbeitsunfälle run through your Berufsgenossenschaft (the DGUV accident-insurance system): the Unfallanzeige is required for injuries causing more than three days' incapacity, and serious/fatal accidents are reported immediately — the insurer then owns treatment and rehabilitation.

Declare the accident du travail to the CPAM within 48 hours (Sundays and holidays excluded) and give the employee the feuille d'accident — the declaration runs electronically and late declarations expose the employer to the costs.

The Employees' Compensation Act and the ESIC scheme carry the duties: ESI-covered units report accidents through ESIC and benefits run from there, while non-covered employment falls under the EC Act's compensation machinery — the labour ministry is the canonical start.

Work accidents route through the employer's mandatory private accident insurance, and serious or fatal accidents must also reach ACT (the labour-conditions authority) within 24 hours — ACT's portal was unreachable to our crawler, so the consolidated labour code is the committed reference.

Reporting clocks are provincial: each workers'-compensation board sets its own employer-report deadline (Ontario's WSIB gives three days), and serious incidents also go to the provincial OHS regulator — CCOHS maintains the board directory.

contextNeeded.query: what happened, to whom, how serious — and when you learned of it (the clocks run from knowledge)
your workers'-comp carrier/policy and the state you operate in

title: Report and manage a workplace injury
description: Take care of the person first. The reporting deadlines are short and run from when you learn of the outcome: a work-related fatality goes to OSHA within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 (rule card us-fed.osha-severe-injury-reporting, osha.gov cited). Then workers' comp. Notify your carrier and get the claim form to the employee fast; state deadlines are short (California requires the DWC-1 within one working day of learning of the injury). Write the incident record while memories are fresh, plus the OSHA 300 log entry if you are covered. Plan the return to work realistically. Fix the hazard. State systems differ sharply; this is the generic shape, so check your own state's rules and fund. Nothing here is legal advice. The claim moves on the carrier's and the state's timelines.

nodes.label: Care first: emergency response, the scene made safe — everything else waits for this
Check the OSHA clocks: fatality — report within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss — within 24
File the OSHA report if a clock applies — by phone or the online form (state-plan states have their own channels)
Notify the workers'-comp carrier and give the employee the claim form — state deadlines are short (CA: DWC-1 within one working day of notice)
Write the incident record while it's fresh: what, where, witnesses, equipment — and the OSHA 300 log entry if you're covered
Plan return-to-work or modified duty honestly, with the employee and the carrier
Fix the hazard and document the correction — the recurrence is the lawsuit
The claim runs on the carrier's and the state's clocks — track it, don't chase it daily

trigger: An employee reports harassment: by complaint, by email, or in a conversation that just became one.
supportReason: The investigation, the proportionate-action judgment, and every conversation in this flow are irreducibly human (and counsel-led where it's senior); an agent can preserve the file and keep the timeline straight.

geoNotes.summary: The ACAS Code of Practice governs grievance handling — a fair procedure (investigation, hearing, appeal) is what tribunals expect, and compensation uplifts of up to 25% apply for unreasonably ignoring the Code.

The AGG gives employees a statutory complaint right (§13) and obliges the employer to act against harassment (§12, up to dismissal of the harasser) — a named complaints body (Beschwerdestelle) is expected in every company.

The Code du travail obliges the employer to prevent and act on harcèlement moral and sexuel; companies of 250+ must designate a référent, the CSE has its own alert rights, and the employer's inaction is itself actionable.

The POSH Act 2013 is statutory machinery, not policy: every workplace with 10+ employees must constitute an Internal Committee, complaints go to the IC, and the inquiry runs on a 90-day clock with annual reporting — the ministry for women and child development administers the regime.

The Código do Trabalho bans harassment outright and companies with seven or more employees must adopt a code of good conduct — investigate promptly and document; complaints can escalate to ACT and assédio carries counter-ordinance fines.

Provincial OHS statutes impose written harassment programs and investigation duties (Ontario's OHSA is the model); federally regulated employers follow the Work Place Harassment and Violence Prevention Regulations with trained investigators.

contextNeeded.query: the complaint as received, and who is involved (conflicts decide the investigator)

title: Respond to a harassment complaint
description: How you respond becomes the company's defense. Make it prompt, thorough, documented. Retaliation is separately unlawful, so draw the no-retaliation line on day one (the EEOC's published employer guidance is the reference). Take the complaint seriously without judging or promising outcomes. Put interim measures in place that protect the complainant rather than punish them. Pick an investigator without conflicts; for anything senior, outside counsel or an external HR investigator. Run the investigation properly. Decide proportionately, up to termination, and document the reasoning. Close the loop with the complainant. Then watch for retaliation for months; that is where companies lose. An EEOC charge may still come; the file you built is what answers it. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

nodes.label: Take it seriously at receipt: acknowledge, no judgments, no promises — and the no-retaliation line drawn on day one (retaliation is separately unlawful)
Interim measures while you investigate — schedule or reporting-line separation chosen to protect the complainant, never to punish them
Choose the investigator: trained and unconflicted internally, or outside counsel / an external HR investigator for anything senior
Run the investigation: interviews, documents, contemporaneous notes — prompt, thorough, documented
Preserve the file: the complaint, interview notes, decisions and their reasons — the file is the company's defense
Decide and act proportionately — up to termination — with the reasoning documented
Close the loop with the complainant (the outcome, not necessarily the details) — and actively watch for retaliation for months
